🎵 What is this music video trying to do?

Start with the big idea. The storyboard frames are already there — now add the meaning, mood and design choices that turn it into a music video.

Song: People Like You — Seb Lowe.
Timing note: This is a best-effort 3-second alignment using the staff-supplied lyric sheet. The storyboard reaches about 2:48, while the song may run a few seconds longer, so check the sync while listening and adjust any lyric box that feels early or late.
Planning focus: each frame now shows the matched lyric line, plus space for the student to add visual meaning, design and production choices.

🎬 Tap the style choices that fit

These choices can guide the frame-by-frame design. Tap as many as fit.

⚡ The creative rule

A good music video usually has a rule that keeps it together: a colour that changes, a repeated prop, a repeated camera movement, a performance space, or a story that develops across the song.

🎞️ Frame-by-frame planner

Each panel is one 3-second moment from the storyboard. The lyric boxes have been prefilled from the supplied lyric sheet, so the student can design how each line becomes a music-video image.

Tip: Use the lyric as the anchor, then decide whether the frame should respond to the exact words, the meaning underneath them, the beat, the mood, or the section change. Fine-tune timings while listening to the track.

✅ Production steps — tap each one when done

This keeps the student moving from planning to filming and editing. Saves on this device.

Before filmingMake the idea shootable
1
Choose the final song section / track
Know the length, tempo and key lyric moments.
✓
2
Complete the frame planner for the opening 30 seconds
At least frames 1–10 should have action, design and camera ideas.
✓
3
List props, costume and locations
Use the Design tab and frame notes to avoid missing anything.
✓
4
Check permissions and safety
Locations, people in shot, trip hazards, filming near roads, copyrighted logos/posters.
✓
During filmingCapture enough material
5
Film the performance base layer
Get full takes or longer sections so the edit has something stable to return to.
✓
6
Film narrative / b-roll inserts
Close-ups, props, movement, locations, cutaways and transitions.
✓
7
Get at least one retake of important moments
Especially chorus, ending, lyric sync and complex camera moves.
✓
EditingMake it feel like a music video
8
Sync key shots to the music
Mark beats, chorus starts, lyric moments and section changes.
✓
9
Add colour / contrast decisions
Keep the visual identity consistent with your colour and lighting plan.
✓
10
Export and review against the storyboard
Check that the beginning, middle and ending actually show the intended progression.
✓
